ranking.note: Raised to P2: in-tree release notes and man pages are a hard prerequisite for tagging 32.0, so delay directly stalls a release cycle.

Raised to P2 and moved up: fixes upgrade instructions that leave users running stale multiprocess binaries and walks back overclaimed privacy guarantees — wrong docs with security/configuration consequences, the top criterion here.
Raised to P2 and moved up for parity with #36319: same wrong upgrade-step fix, same user consequence, on the 30.x branch.
Moved down: valuable internal-only developer notes, but every PR above it either blocks a release, settles a cross-subsystem convention, or corrects user-facing text.

Raised to P4→P3: the guideline currently contradicts the codebase (only 58 of 129 LogError calls are fatal) and keeps re-opening the same debate in logging PRs, which is a recurring developer burden rather than cosmetic.

inconsistencies: #36319 (31.x) and #36401 (30.x) backport the same upgrade-guide fix (#36441) and bips.md addition (#36377) to different maintenance branches; they are the same problem twice and should be reviewed together, #36319 first since it additionally carries the private-broadcast experimental/claims wording.

#35518 and #35480 are by the same author and both partially close issue #14278 (notification semantics). Review #35518 first: it establishes the general -*notify asynchrony/no-ordering framing that #35480's ZMQ-specific reorg/eviction documentation sits under.

#35858 (new doc/privacy.md, which moves privacy guidance out of doc/tor.md and doc/i2p.md and documents -privatebroadcast) overlaps #36348 (adds -privatebroadcast transient-address text to doc/i2p.md). Decide placement first via #35858, otherwise #36348 adds text to a file whose privacy section is being relocated.

#36319 also tempers private-broadcast privacy claims in released docs, which is the same subject matter as #35858 and #36348 on master; the wording chosen on the maintenance branch should not contradict the master-side consolidation.

All four fanquake/release-branch and release-finalization items are documentation-only by content, so none of them was downgraded for being routine; their priority rests on blocking the release or on correcting user-facing upgrade steps.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: release-blocking/wrong-user-facing-text at P2, and new or consolidated reference documentation at P3. No P1 — nothing here documents something that would mislead a user into losing funds or breaking security configuration in a currently shipped release; the closest, the stale-libexec upgrade step, is already fixed on master and only awaiting backport.
